site.name: aeroiq
site.summary: AeroIQ Fictional API monitoring and observability SaaS (Datadog / Vercel Observability-style). Pages - `index.html` — Overview dashboard. Left rail nav; top bar with org switcher, environment tabs (Production / Staging / Dev), time range (5m / 1h / 24h / 7d), search (⌘K), theme toggle, alert bell; four top KPIs (total requests / error rate / p95 / availability) with sparklines and period-over-period deltas; 24-card endpoint health grid (red cards first), each card with HTTP method + path + health dot + RPS / p95 / error rate; right alerts side panel with 8 active alerts and per-row assign / silence actions; bottom global p50 / p95 / p99 trend line chart. - `endpoint-detail.html` — Endpoint detail. Top: method + path + health badge + linked services + owner avatars; 6 KPIs (RPS / error rate / p50 / p95 / p99 / SLO status); three large trend charts (request volume, latency p50/p95/p99 three lines, error rate); error-grouping panel with status-code / client-version / region tabs; recent error sample table (5 rows including 502 Bad Gateway, 500, 429, 503); related traces list. - `alerts.html` — Alerts center. 4 KPIs (active / new today / mean response / MTTR); filter bar; 12-row alert

run_plan.goal: Autonomously explore and critique the AeroIQ observability workflow end-to-end, centering on the dashboard-to-investigation path and covering adjacent monitoring pages, filters, and responsive behavior.
run_plan.summary: Start on the overview dashboard and validate the primary triage flow: scan KPIs, inspect the endpoint health grid, use the active alerts panel, and move into a problematic endpoint for deeper diagnosis. Then cover the adjacent operational pages—Endpoints, Alerts, and Service Map—by exercising their visible filters, navigation, and state toggles. Finish with focused mobile checks on the top navigation, dense controls, and alert/endpoint triage surfaces, since the prescan already shows likely tap-target and labeling issues.
assumptions: The core user journey is dashboard triage leading into endpoint investigation, supported by alerts and endpoint list pages.
Only five HTML pages are known and should be treated as the primary coverage scope: index.html, endpoints.html, endpoint-detail.html, alerts.html, and services.html.
Logs, Integrations, and Settings links appear to be placeholders (#) and should be noted but not treated as real destination coverage.
Environment tabs, time-range tabs, theme toggle, org switcher, filters, and alert actions are visible controls worth exercising, but no backend persistence should be assumed in this local demo.
Search is present on several pages; validate interaction and UX behavior without assuming full command-palette behavior beyond what is visibly exposed.
risk_hotspots: index.html: dense top bar with org switcher, environment tabs, time-range tabs, search, theme toggle, bell, and profile competing for space and discoverability
index.html: endpoint health grid with 24 cards sorted by health; needs validation for scanability, click affordance, and transition into detail
index.html: right-side Active Alerts panel with per-row Assign and Silence actions; high-risk for cramped actions and unclear state change
endpoint-detail.html: unhealthy POST /v1/payments investigation page with multiple KPI panels, three charts, and error tabs; needs information hierarchy validation
endpoint-detail.html: Error breakdown tabs (status code / client version / region) and recent error sample table; verify tab switching clarity and cross-panel consistency
endpoints.html: high-density endpoint table with multiple filters (service, health, tag, search); validate filter combinations and whether unhealthy rows remain easy to find
alerts.html: filter bar plus 12-row alert table with statuses Open/Assigned/Resolved; check whether filtering and search support recovery workflows
services.html: service node interaction is implied by copy ('Click a service node to view details'); validate whether nodes are actually interactive and understandable
Global mobile risk: many visible controls are below recommended tap-target size, especially nav items and top-bar tabs/buttons
Global accessibility risk: unlabeled select controls were flagged in prescan on multiple pages

phases.title: Dashboard triage and primary navigation
phases.objective: Validate the overview dashboard as the main entry point for detecting issues and choosing the next investigative step.
key_checks: Confirm left-rail navigation reaches all known real pages: Dashboard, Endpoints, Alerts, Service Map
Inspect KPI cards and verify time-range controls (5m, 1h, 24h, 7d) visibly update selection and remain understandable
Inspect environment tabs (Production, Staging, Dev) for clear active state and any page-level data/state changes
Exercise org switcher and confirm whether changing org affects visible context without breaking layout
Use the search input and assess discoverability, placeholder clarity, and whether entered queries produce visible feedback
Open or interact with the bell/profile/theme controls if possible and note any overlays, dead controls, or ambiguous affordances
Assess whether the dashboard makes the most urgent unhealthy endpoints and active alerts obvious at a glance
exit_criteria: Dashboard top-bar controls have been exercised at least once each where possible
All known primary nav links from the dashboard have been verified
A clear next-step path from dashboard triage into either alerts or endpoint investigation has been identified

phases.title: Issue drill-down from dashboard to endpoint detail
phases.objective: Follow the most critical monitoring flow from a problematic dashboard card or alert into detailed endpoint diagnosis.
key_checks: Attempt entry into endpoint-detail.html from the unhealthy endpoint cards or alerts-related affordances, preferring POST /v1/payments or POST /v1/webhooks/stripe if reachable
On endpoint detail, verify the page header communicates method, path, health, service ownership, and severity clearly
Exercise time-range controls again on the detail page and check whether chart labels/selected states stay coherent
Review request volume, latency, and error rate charts for readability and whether comparative signals are easy to interpret
Switch error breakdown tabs (By status code, By client version, By region) and confirm content changes are obvious and useful
Inspect recent error samples and related traces for scanability, truncation, and connection to the error-breakdown context
Judge whether a user can move from symptom to probable cause quickly on this page
exit_criteria: At least one full dashboard-to-detail investigative path has been completed
All major content regions on endpoint-detail.html have been interacted with or reviewed
Potential confusion points in charts, tabs, or error diagnostics have been captured

phases.title: Endpoints inventory and filtering workflow
phases.objective: Validate the endpoint catalog as a secondary investigation and monitoring surface.
key_checks: Open endpoints.html from navigation and assess first-glance scanability of the 32-endpoint table
Exercise visible filters: service, health, tag, and search method/path
Try filter combinations that isolate unhealthy/breached endpoints and confirm whether the table remains understandable
Inspect whether service names, health, SLO, last deploy, and owner columns support prioritization
Attempt to open an endpoint from the table into endpoint-detail.html and compare the transition quality against the dashboard entry path
Check whether global search and page-level search are differentiated clearly enough
exit_criteria: Each visible filter on endpoints.html has been used at least once
At least one filtered state and one cleared/default state have been reviewed
A table-to-detail navigation path has been validated or clearly identified as missing

phases.title: Alerts triage and recovery actions
phases.objective: Evaluate the dedicated alerts workflow for prioritization, assignment, silencing, and finding specific incidents.
key_checks: Open alerts.html from nav and compare the full alerts center against the dashboard side panel summary
Review KPI cards (active, new today, avg response time, MTTR) for clarity and usefulness
Exercise filter bar controls: severity, rules, assignees, status, and search
Try common triage views such as Critical only, Open only, or a specific assignee if options allow
Inspect the alert rows for readability of time, rule, endpoint, severity, status, and owner
Use any visible Assign/Silence actions where available and note whether feedback/state change is clear
Confirm whether 'view all' from the dashboard lands users in the expected alerts context
exit_criteria: All visible alert filters have been exercised at least once
At least one alert action has been attempted where actionable controls are exposed
The relationship between dashboard alerts summary and full alerts center has been assessed

phases.title: Service map comprehension and responsive validation
phases.objective: Check the service topology page and then repeat critical flows on mobile to surface layout and touch issues.
key_checks: Open services.html and verify whether Production/Staging toggles visibly affect the map
Attempt interaction with service nodes, since the page explicitly invites clicking a node to view details
Assess whether service relationships, traffic weighting, and labels are understandable without zoom or hover-only cues
Repeat high-priority checks on mobile viewport for index.html: nav access, top-bar controls, search, time ranges, endpoint cards, and alert panel
Repeat focused mobile checks on alerts.html and endpoints.html filters/search because these pages have dense controls and unlabeled selects
Check for clipped content, overlap, hidden controls, off-canvas nav issues, and usability problems caused by small tap targets
exit_criteria: services.html has been visited and its visible interactive promises have been validated
Critical dashboard, alerts, and endpoints interactions have been rechecked on mobile
Mobile-specific issues around tap targets, labels, and crowded control bars have been documented

coverage_targets.pages: Visit all 5 known HTML pages, with repeated visits to index.html and endpoint-detail.html for the main triage flow.
coverage_targets.features: Exercise most visible controls on the dashboard, endpoint detail, endpoints filters, alerts filters/actions, service-map environment toggles, and global nav/search/theme controls where present.
coverage_targets.mobile: Repeat the critical triage flow and dense-control pages on a mobile viewport, prioritizing nav access, top-bar controls, endpoint cards/table filters, and alerts interactions.

notes: Do not spend significant time on Logs, Integrations, or Settings unless they unexpectedly resolve to real destinations, because prescan shows placeholder links.
Prefer investigating the clearly unhealthy endpoints surfaced in prescan: POST /v1/payments and POST /v1/webhooks/stripe.
Because max_steps is 80, aim for full page coverage plus selective state permutations rather than exhaustive combinations of every filter value.
Capture whether global controls behave consistently across pages, especially org switcher, search, environment tabs, and notification bell.

ux_notes: Clicking the inline 'Assign' action did open a modal titled 'Assign alert' with the helper text 'Open assign modal for: POST /v1/payments,' so the action is not a silent no-op and provides immediate context-specific feedback.
The confirmation flow appears incomplete: the modal only offers 'Cancel' and 'Confirm' with no visible assignee picker or owner details, which may leave users unsure what 'Confirm' will actually do.
The Active Alerts panel is visually cramped, and the inline actions are small (e.g. 'Assign' is 57x24px), which weakens confidence for frequent triage actions even though the click succeeded.

step.objective: Learn whether the ambiguous assign confirmation produces clear success/state change or undermines trust by performing an unexplained action.
step.success_criteria: A visible assigned state, owner update, toast, or modal outcome appears; otherwise the lack of explicit result exposes weak confirmation UX.

ux_notes: The dashboard’s 'view all →' link reliably opens the full alerts center (URL changed from index.html# to alerts.html), and orientation is preserved because the destination keeps the same left-rail nav with '🚨 Alerts 8' highlighted plus matching alert summary context ('Active 8' appears on the alerts page).

ux_notes: Clicking the Alerts rail link to Endpoints successfully changed the URL from alerts.html to endpoints.html and loaded a clearly oriented Endpoints page with the left-nav highlight, an 'Endpoints' heading, and immediate inventory controls (service/health/tag filters plus 'Search method or path…').

The destination feels like a natural next step from alert triage because the table foregrounds problem endpoints first with health dots, error %, SLO breach states, owners, and recent deploy times (for example /v1/payments and /v1/webhooks/stripe show red health and breach status), supporting comparison against alert investigations.

Some investigation context is not preserved across the transition: the Endpoints page resets to broad defaults ('All services', 'All health', 'tag: any') and there is no visible carryover of any alert-specific filter, selected endpoint, or breadcrumb from Alerts.

step.objective: Learn whether selecting an unhealthy-only view on the Endpoints page gives clear, trustworthy filtering feedback that helps users focus on incidents.
step.success_criteria: The health selector visibly changes to Unhealthy and the table reduces to the red/problem rows, revealing whether the filter meaningfully supports triage.

ux_notes: Dashboard loaded successfully as the responsive validation starting point, showing the dense triage layout with left nav, top control bar, KPI cards, endpoint grid, and right-side Active Alerts panel all visible on desktop.

The top bar is already crowded before mobile testing: org select, 3 environment tabs, 4 time-range buttons, search, theme, bell, and profile are all present in one row, indicating likely compression risk on smaller screens.

Several controls are under mobile tap-size guidance even on desktop measurements, including left-nav items at 195x41px and environment buttons like Production at 91x28px and Staging at 71x28px, which is concrete evidence of likely touch usability issues.
The org switcher select is flagged with a missing label/aria-label in layout warnings, indicating an accessibility issue in a key global control.

step.objective: Learn whether changing the org switcher gives clear, trustworthy feedback about global context or feels inert/ambiguous like some other top-bar controls.
step.success_criteria: The selected org should visibly change and ideally trigger corresponding dashboard/context updates, revealing whether the global context switch is understandable and trustworthy.

result.feedback: Selected option 'Acme Internal'. No obvious URL or visible-text change was detected after the action.

The org switcher select has a medium-severity accessibility issue: it is flagged with a missing label, which weakens clarity for a control meant to change global context.

step.objective: Learn whether selecting the 7d dashboard time range gives clear visual feedback or, like other global controls, feels inert and undermines trust in the monitoring context.
step.success_criteria: The 7d control becomes visibly active and dashboard KPI/chart context updates to 7d, or the absence of change provides evidence of broken/inert time filtering.

ux_notes: Clicking the 7d button produced a visible state change, but the dashboard context stayed on 1h: visible text still shows 'Total Requests · 1h' and heading 'Global latency (p50 / p95 / p99) · 1h', so the global time filter appears selected without propagating to KPI/chart labels.

This mismatch between the active-looking 7d control and unchanged 1h metric context is concrete evidence of inert or inconsistently wired global filtering, which can undermine trust in a monitoring dashboard.

step.objective: Learn whether switching from the misleading 7d-selected state to 5m updates KPI/chart context coherently or further confirms broken global timeframe behavior.
step.success_criteria: The 5m control should become active and dashboard headings/KPIs should change to 5m context; if labels remain at 1h, that provides stronger evidence of inconsistent time filtering UX.

result.feedback: Visible content changed after the action.

ux_notes: The click missed the intended unhealthy endpoint-card investigation flow and instead activated an alert-row 'Assign' button, opening a modal dialog titled 'Assign alert' with copy 'Open assign modal for: POST /v1/payments'.

This reveals a triage affordance risk on the dashboard: alert actions sit alongside the endpoint health grid, and the action did not transition to an investigation/detail page; URL stayed on index.html and the page now shows a blocking dialog with Confirm/Cancel instead.

step.objective: Learn whether the assign-alert modal has a straightforward cancel/recovery path that returns users to normal triage without side effects.
step.success_criteria: The modal closes and the dashboard returns to its normal state, revealing whether accidental alert-action activation is easy to recover from.

result.feedback: No obvious URL or visible-text change was detected after the action.

The tool also reported no visible-text or URL change after the click, which reinforces that Cancel provides weak or ambiguous feedback about whether the action succeeded.

step.objective: Verify whether a simple page reload cleanly clears the lingering assign-alert modal and returns the dashboard to a trustworthy baseline for further UX evaluation.

ux_notes: The page reopened in desktop, not mobile: new_observation.viewport is "desktop", so this action did not validate crowded controls or navigation access in a mobile context.

Even in desktop, the top bar is control-dense with org select, 3 environment buttons, 4 time-range buttons, search, theme toggle, bell, and profile all on one row, suggesting likely crowding risk when reduced to mobile width.

Tooling surfaced concrete usability issues relevant to mobile readiness: multiple nav links are only 41px tall (e.g. Dashboard/Endpoints/Alerts/Service Map/Logs/Integrations/Settings) and header chips are 28px tall (Production/Staging), both below 44px guidance.
Accessibility evidence also shows the org switcher select lacks a label/aria-label per layout warning, which weakens clarity for assistive tech and form comprehension.

step.objective: Determine whether the top unhealthy endpoint card on the dashboard behaves like an obvious navigation target into endpoint investigation, rather than forcing users to use side navigation or alerts.
step.success_criteria: Either the click opens a detail/investigation state, or it reveals that the dashboard’s nearby actions are easier to hit than the endpoint cards themselves, which is useful UX evidence about affordance and misclick risk.
